newsitem.title: UK: British sculptor charged with stealing body parts.
newsitem.headline: British sculptor charged with stealing body parts.

text.p: A butcher-turned-sculptor with connections to Britain's royal family has been charged with stealing human body parts and using them in his art, police said on Tuesday.

Anthony-Noel Kelly, a cousin of the Duke of Norfolk and a part-time teacher at Prince Charles's Institute of Architecture, and another man who was a former employee of the Royal College of Surgeons, were charged with theft.

"They are due to appear in court on August 15 charged with theft of various anatomical parts belonging to the Royal College of Surgeons between June 1991 and November 1994," a police spokesman told Reuters.
Kelly, 41, was arrested in April after police discovered 30 human body parts in raids on his London studio and country home.
Police launched the investigation following a request from the government's Inspector of Anatomy, Dr Lawrence Martin.
Kelly, who has said he found beauty in death, won recognition for his moulds of heads, feet and torsos which he said was his way of immortalising the dead.
Some of his works which were gilded in gold and silver sold for thousands of pounds (dollars).
